newsitem.title: INDIA: Former Indian PM Rao charged in vote-buying case.
newsitem.headline: Former Indian PM Rao charged in vote-buying case.

text.p: An Indian court indicted former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and 19 others on Tuesday in a bribes-for-votes case, his lawyer and court officials said.

Judge Ajit Bharihoke of a special court of inquiry in the capital ruled there was sufficient evidence to try Rao for criminal conspiracy and abetment to bribery, the counsel for the former prime minister, R.K. Anand, told Reuters.
Both charges carry a maximum penalty of five years in prison if the accused is convicted, Anand said.
Bharihoke set May 14 for arraignment when the accused will be asked to enter a plea. A trial would follow for those who plead not guilty.

Anand said Rao was innocent in the case involving allegations that in 1993, he tried to influence a parliamentary vote of no-confidence by bribing four deputies of a tribespeople's party in the eastern state of Bihar.
Rao's minority government defeated the no-confidence motion by a narrow margin.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has been investigating payments totalling three million rupees ($84,000) made into a bank account held by a member of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) party.

The CBI had already charged Rao and the others in the vote-buying case. The special court judge on Tuesday agreed that there was adequate evidence to proceed to trial and framed charges against Rao and the others, a CBI spokesman said.
Rao, who led his Congress party to its worst-ever defeat in general elections last year, has been named in two other criminal cases relating to forgery and cheating.
He has denied wrongdoing in all of the cases and has obtained preventive bail in all three, which are before courts in New Delhi.
Rao quit as Congress chief last September after a judge ordered him to appear in court in the criminal cheating case.

Anand said Bharihoke rejected a legal request that the court summon the current Congress president, Sitaram Kesri, in the vote-buying case. Kesri had been accused by one of the JMM leaders who allegedly received a bribe.
Among the 19 others accused in the case were several former government ministers and leading political figures. All have denied involvement in the case.
Anand said he would file a petition asking the Delhi High Court to discharge the vote-buying charges against Rao on the grounds that there was insufficient evidence. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
